subjects.displayTitle: Judaism and the Torah: inheritance, interpretation, and universal hope
subjects.introduction: Israel, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, must now set its thoughts on what benefits all humanity, for today whatever is particular ends in loss and whatever is universal is divine. He tells his own followers to honour the Jewish believers as descendants of Abraham and to kiss their faces on his behalf; he prays that a scattered and oppressed people be gathered and glorified; and he reads the Mosaic revelation as the education that raised a nation from abasement to glory. He also presses on inherited interpretations: the Torah survives in three versions that disagree on chronology, chosenness means service and sacrifice rather than privilege, and expected signs of a Messiah have more than once stood between a people and its promise. Some of this is polemic or reported conversation, and speaks for its source rather than for Jewish life today. Isaiah’s vision of the nations streaming to instruction and beating swords into ploughshares holds the same horizon in the Hebrew Bible’s own words [1]. The way leads on to Moses and Abraham, to progressive revelation, and to the interpretation of the Bible.
subjects.arc: Begin with universal benefit and the spiritual dignity of Israel, explore prophetic inheritance and scripture, then examine interpretation, renewal, and the responsibilities of religious hope.

order.why: Consider the reported interpretation of being chosen as responsibility and service.
shortened: Question:	The American turns to the Master: "Honoured Teacher, what does the Prophet of the Baha'i Religion teach regarding the future of Israel, will Israel remain the Chosen People - until the end of time?"
Answer:	The Master explains: "The word 'chosen' (in English) is easily regarded as meaning the same as 'favoured', 'spoiled', 'elect', 'before others'.

By whom have the Jews been chosen? We are agreed on this -by God, the Almighty! For what, to what purpose have they been chosen: for service, for sacrificial service, and because service and sacrifice are synonymous with suffering, the answer is: God, the All-Highest, has chosen the people of Israel for service and for suffering.

order.why: Consider the reported unity of the religions of Moses and Baha’u’llah.
Open with the call to benefit all humanity beyond particular interests.
shortened: His bounty will overshadow them, and this race will day by day progress, and be delivered from its age-long obscurity and degradation.

What is universal today is divine and causes the progress of all humanity, while what is particular is pure detriment and sheer loss. Now Israel must set aside infirm notions and, with a sound purpose, concern itself with matters universal. Israel's thoughts must settle on what benefits all and brings happiness to all humanity.

order.why: Hear prayer for an oppressed people and gratitude for its prophetic inheritance.
shortened: O Lord, God of Abraham and Isaac! Thou hast clothed this glorious party of Israel in the robe of virtue and distinguished them with a special gift, and made them the manifestation of "Verily, I have chosen you above all peoples." From that people Thou didst raise up Prophets and gather blessed souls beneath the shadow of the Most Great Banner. O Lord! Make manifest and evident that which Thou didst promise through the tongue of the Prophets, and make them successful and joyous through the gifts which Thou didst give them glad tidings of. Grant organization to this scattered people and bestow eternal glory upon this oppressed nation, that they may gather in the Holy Land which is the inheritance of their forefathers and with utmost glory engage in Thy praise and glorification.

order.why: Read the educational power attributed to the Mosaic revelation.
shortened: The essence of the matter is this: When His Holiness Moses the Great delivered Israel from ancient Egypt and brought them to the Holy Land, through the power of God's law, the force of God's Kingdom, the breaths of prophetic revelation, and the education of the pure ones, Israel ascended from the depths of abasement to the heights of glory in both worlds. They progressed in all degrees of existence until, in the time of David and Solomon, they reached such a station that the fame of their nobility reached all horizons and news of their virtues and qualities reached East and West.

order.why: Read the injunction to honor Jewish believers through the memory of the prophets.
shortened: Extend utmost respect and honor to the Jewish believers, descendants of Abraham, on my behalf and kiss their faces and hair, for they heard the counsels of Abraham with the ear of the soul and carried them out with heart and limb.

Moses the Interlocutor counts that people as the manifestation of great grace. Aaron knows Israel as the manifestations of the favors of the Incomparable Lord. Solomon considers his people as successful in both worlds. David sees the Jews as manifestations of the favors of the Loving Lord. Isaiah, Elijah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Ezra all praise and commend all of Israel.

order.why: Hear the synagogue address’s appeal to mutual recognition of prophets.
Retain the reported account of growth under the Mosaic law.
shortened: That is, the Word of God bestowed the spirit of faith upon the children of Israel, and that nation advanced in all degrees under the shadow of His Law and expanded until the time of Solomon and David, taking five hundred years before the Cause was spread as it should be.

order.why: Read the divine name through the passage’s use of Exodus.
Explore the reported consequences of Abraham’s journey.
shortened: However, the migration and wandering of Abraham resulted in the guidance of the entire world and precipitated the Manifestation of Isaac, Ishmael, Jacob, Joseph, Moses, David, Solomon, Christ, Muhammad and the Exalted One [the Bab].

order.why: Keep the reported account of Melchisedec and Abraham attributed.
Read the reported connection of prophetic histories with the Holy Land.
shortened: Abraham was in Haran, but at last he was brought to this place, and the King of Peace, the teacher of Abraham, was here. Moses was here in these surroundings. The prophets of Israel all were here. Jesus Christ was also from here and Mohammed emigrated to this place, and this new Revelation also came to this place; although He originated in Persia, the Blessed Perfection came to this place.

order.why: Consider dreams within the reported account of Israel’s prophets.
Read the reported division after Solomon and Elijah’s renewal.
Retain the reported interpretation of Elijah’s withdrawal.
Keep the related account of the fiery chariot in its reported setting.
Read the reported accounts of Moses’s and Elijah’s final days.
Keep the reported history of idolatry and renewal attributed.
Retain the reported childhood story of Moses without treating it as verified history.
Read the brief reported account of Moses’s prophetic claim.
shortened: Moses, outwardly, struck and killed a man, then came and said "I am he who killed that man, and now I have become a Prophet."

order.why: Consider the address’s use of Moses’s poverty as a moral example.
shortened: "All the prophets of God were poor, His Holiness Moses was a mere shepherd. This will show you that in the estimation of God, poverty is greater than the accumulation of wealth--that the poor are more acceptable than the lazy rich.

order.why: Hear the association of carpentry with Noah’s service.
Read the allusion to Solomon’s prayer for sovereignty.
Keep the reported hoopoe image in its own narrative tradition.
Consider the reported endurance of Joseph’s beauty and the disciples’ honor.
shortened: But the fame of the beauty of Joseph is still universal and the honor of the disciples of Christ still endures; their sufferings are the cause of life everlasting.

order.why: Read the reported explanation of filial language in scripture.
Consider the account of the term Israel and its expanding meaning.
shortened: But regarding the word Israel, this is the title of Jacob himself and not that of his Children.  Then from the word of "Bani Israel" Bani (descendants) was dropped and they sufficed with the word "Israel."

Afterward the word Israel was used to denote the "people of God" as it is mentioned in the Bible, i.e., the nations of God.  Thus it was gradually generalized as to denote all the souls who accepted the religion of God.

order.why: Hear the cited affirmation of divine favor.
shortened: His exalted Word states: "O Children of Israel! Remember My favor wherewith I favored you and how I preferred you above all creatures."

order.why: Introduce the discussion of biblical versions through its concrete comparison.
shortened: Furthermore, the Torah, held to be the most ancient of histories, existeth today in three separate versions: the Hebrew, considered authentic by the Jews and the Protestant clergy; the Greek Septuagint, which is used as authoritative in the Greek and other Eastern churches; and the Samaritan Torah, the standard authority for that people. These three versions differ greatly, one from another, even with regard to the lifetimes of the most celebrated figures.

order.why: Read the distinction between collected prophetic sayings and historical accounts.
shortened: They have gathered various sayings of the Prophets like Isaiah, Ezekiel, Solomon, David, Jeremiah, Zechariah and others into one volume, though most parts of it are historical accounts written after Moses.

order.why: Explore the distinction between Mosaic laws and historical narrative.
shortened: Regarding the matter of Judas, and the matter of David, and the matter of Noah, and other matters recorded in the Torah - know that the Torah has two parts: one part historical and one part divine laws and religious ordinances. The section of laws and ordinances is from His Eminence Moses, but the historical section is from Ezra. Proof of this is that at the end of the fifth book, events that occurred after Moses are recorded, and it is clear as the sun that events after Moses were recorded by someone else.

order.why: Consider interpretation and translation alongside uncertainty about deliberate additions.
Keep the reported account of Pentateuchal authorship attributed.
Read the related reported appeal to historical discrepancies as its own argument.
Retain the reported identification of Torah and Deuteronomy in its particular setting.
shortened: He stated that this is so, but the Torah that is in the hands of people is not the complete heavenly Book. For instance, it states 'Moses said thus.' What has this to do with a heavenly Book, and what has something written after Moses to do with Moses? These are additions that historians have appended to the Torah. The Torah is that Book of Deuteronomy which contains the laws.

order.why: Read the reported distinction between inspired writings and historical books.
shortened: The only parts of the Bible we should consider as sacred and inspired are these revealed writings and visions. With regard to the Book of Moses, only those parts are sacred which contain his inspired writings, such as the Ten Commandments, etc. The rest are mere books of history written much later than the time of Moses and often not literally true.

order.why: Preserve the recorded corrections in the reported comparison of biblical versions.
Keep the polemical judgment about the David story in its source’s voice.
Consider religious law and reason through this passage’s example.
shortened: Now, the question of the excellence or baseness of things is determined either by reason or by religious law. Some believe that it is based on religious law: Such is the case with the Jews, who believe that all the commandments of the Torah are binding and that they are matters of religious law rather than of reason. Thus they say that one of the commandments of the Torah is that meat and butter cannot be eaten together, for this is "trefah" (and "trefah" in Hebrew means unclean, while "kosher" means clean). This they say is a question of religious law and not of reason.

order.why: Retain the reported description of fasting without generalizing it as Jewish practice.
shortened: 'ABDUL-BAHA: In the Torah the command for fasting is from sunset to sunset for three days. For three days and three nights they, the Jews, take nothing. This is not obligatory. There are Fasts of three days, seven days and nine days.

order.why: Read the specific instruction concerning the daughter within its limited context.
Consider the reported discussion of changing legal circumstances.
shortened: Likewise, the physical laws and transactions of the Torah suited that time. They cannot be implemented now. There are ten death sentences in the Torah - can they be carried out? For instance, can someone who takes out another's eye have their own eyes removed? Can someone who throws a stone breaking another's tooth have their tooth broken with a stone? Can one who curses their father be put to death? Even before the time of the Messenger of God, the Israelites had suspended these laws.

order.why: Keep the reported legal assertions attributed rather than treating them as a survey of Torah law.
Discusses allusive references in the Torah and their interpretation.
Read the account of Christ’s emergence as this text’s theological history.
shortened: Briefly, this Man, Who appeared lowly in the eyes of all, arose nonetheless with such power as to abrogate a fifteen-hundred-year-old Dispensation, notwithstanding that the least deviation from its laws would expose the offender to grave danger and bring about his death and annihilation. Moreover, in the time of Christ the general morals and manners of the Israelites had become entirely confused and corrupted, and Israel had fallen into a state of utmost degradation, misery, and bondage.

order.why: Explore the account of messianic expectations and literal signs.
shortened: The reason for this was that they said: "The Revelation of Christ, according to the clear text of the Torah, will be attested by certain signs, and so long as these signs have not appeared, whoso layeth claim to be a Messiah is an impostor. Among these signs is this, that the Messiah should come from an unknown place, yet we all know this man's house in Nazareth, and can any good thing come out of Nazareth? The second sign is that He shall rule with a rod of iron, that is, He must act with the sword, but this Messiah has not even a wooden staff. Another of the conditions and signs is this: He must sit upon the throne of David and establish David's sovereignty. Now, far from being enthroned, this man has not even a mat to sit on.

order.why: Read the further rhetorical catalogue of expected signs.
Consider the Book of Certitude’s challenge to constructed expectations.
shortened: These people of Israel are even unto the present day still expecting that Manifestation which the Bible hath foretold! How many Manifestations of Holiness, how many Revealers of the light everlasting, have appeared since the time of Moses, and yet Israel, wrapt in the densest veils of satanic fancy and false imaginings, is still expectant that the idol of her own handiwork will appear with such signs as she herself hath conceived!

order.why: Keep the reported story of changing predictions in its original setting.
shortened: The Master continued with a story of the Jewish rabbis:

In Jerusalem every now and then they broadcast a promise giving a specific time based on the holy scriptures and say that on such a date the Promised One will appear to deliver the Jews. They say, 'We have derived these from the holy texts.' But when that time and day approach they cast a doubt over their promise and give another. Thus they keep the Jews under the influence of their wish and desires and deprive them of the truth.

order.why: Read the reported exchange with Ismael as a particular conversation.
Preserve the reported story and its source omission without adding missing narrative.
Read the reported discussion of scriptural and intellectual proofs.
Keep the reported example of a commentary by two children attributed.
Read opposition to Moses as a warning about recognition.
shortened: O Rahim! His Holiness Moses appeared with mighty signs, yet they did not accept Him. Each day He manifested with a proof, a clear evidence, and verses revealed, yet still the opposers and deniers acted without justice or fairness, until the cry "the hosts of God, they shall be victorious!" was raised from the horizon of divine triumph and the banners of victory were planted upon the loftiest stations.

order.why: Consider the repeated appeal to remember the Interlocutor.
Keep the polemical citation about the hand of God within the prayer’s voice.
Read the related concise rejection of a constrained divine power.
Consider the passage’s challenge to austerity without acceptance.
shortened: Even now there are some Jews who have secluded themselves in Jerusalem and are engaged in extreme austerities and scripture reading, with some fasting for three consecutive days and nights, yet they are and shall remain rejected in the sight of God.

order.why: Retain the reported rebuke through its cited scriptural episodes.
Keep the reported explanation of calamities attributed.
Read the reported observation of devotion in Tiberias as a limited personal account.
Consider the text’s description of longing for the Temple.
Keep the reported description of the wall and its accusation attributed.
Read the reported judgment of political motives in its own historical voice.
shortened: They are weeping because their sovereignty is taken away; while the Temple of Solomon has been destroyed. They are longing to try to establish Jewish sovereignty. They are not weeping for the sake of God... of Christ, but for sovereignty; they want worldly power.. to regain their former power and influence.

order.why: Retain the reported contrast among expectations without turning it into a present-day description.
shortened: The Orthodox Jews according to the literal interpretation of a number of passages in the Old Testament, of course are holding such a belief but the growing literary and intellectual party, having cast away the enthusiasm born out of ignorance, discredit the whole proposition as nothing else but a dream. They think it is no more than a wild fancy on the part of the Jews to ever harbor the idea of founding the Solomonic Sovereignty in Jerusalem.

order.why: Consider the reported Ancient Covenant through the transformation it anticipates.
shortened: The essence of the Torah is the Ancient Covenant, and that Ancient Covenant was a harbinger of this new Covenant, which is the Covenant of the manifestation of the Lord with all His attributes and perfection.
It is a Covenant taken from all the Prophets, whereby the face of the earth shall be transformed into the supreme Paradise and the divine signs shall become manifest throughout the world.

order.why: Read the appeal to signs and the promise of honor.
shortened: O descendant of Abraham! If the Israelites look with fairness, they will see that all the signs have appeared. Matters that were impossible and inconceivable have come to pass, and the Lord of Hosts without armies has conquered East and West. The divine law will soon glorify Israel, and the blessed favors will ennoble Abraham's lineage.

order.why: Hear the hope for release from oppression and renewed flourishing.
shortened: In this Most Great Revelation, Israel has become the manifestation of the favors of the Glorious Lord. Therefore, throughout all regions, day by day it grows more honored. A special gaze of divine favor has been directed toward those oppressed ones, so that they may be delivered from their profound abasement, attain eternal glory, and make the desolate Holy Land prosperous and flourishing once again.
And this will undoubtedly come to pass, for the promises that God made through the tongue of the Prophets to this scattered and dispersed people will be fulfilled in this Most Great Cycle.

order.why: Consider the promise that abasement will become honor.
shortened: The meaning is that the abasement which Israel endured for two thousand five hundred years shall now be transformed into eternal glory, and outwardly too they shall become honored, to such a degree that they shall be envied by their enemies and coveted by their friends.

order.why: Read the assurance concerning the children of Jacob.
Keep the account of changes in Iran in its historical setting.
shortened: The Israelites in Iran were in the utmost abasement, but from the day the Sun of Truth dawned upon that land, Israel progressed day by day, gained honor and found comfort, to such a degree that they became the envy of others.

order.why: Retain the reported return and sovereignty predictions as reported claims.
shortened: This land is Palestine. It is a Holy Land. Soon the Jewish people shall return to this land, and once more David's sovereignty and Solomon's splendor shall be made manifest. This is an explicit divine promise, and there is no doubt therein. The Jewish people will be made resplendent. They will gather under the banner of the Cause.

order.why: Read the related brief reported prediction.
shortened: The sovereignty of David and the splendor of Solomon will once more be manifested.

order.why: Keep the reported return and conversion claims attributed.
Read the later reported recollection of promises concerning the Holy Land.
shortened: He said: "In their heavenly books the prophets have spoken of the Day of the Lord, the Last Day, and what they have spoken is all being realized in this day. The Blessed Beauty sixty years ago in some of his tablets promised the Jews that they would come back to the Holy Land and what he said will be realized.

order.why: Hear the reported invitation to witness the land’s flourishing.
Retain the reported answer about the scattered tribes.
Keep the reported conversion numbers and forecast distinct from verified statistics.
Retain the related reported numerical generalization without endorsing it.
Read the reported statement about future acceptance in its source’s voice.
shortened: It is the destiny of the Jewish people to embrace the Cause - a fact of which there is no doubt.

order.why: Keep the brief reported forecast within its own context.
shortened: Perchance it is because of this that Jewish people will embrace the Cause, since there is no other course left to them.

order.why: Return to service and the hoped-for joy of the prophets.
shortened: Praise be to God that in this Most Great Cycle the glance of grace encompasses Israel so that all the promises of the Prophets regarding them may be fulfilled in the world of existence and witness.

Therefore my hope is firm that the friends of Israel will render a notable service at this time to the Glorious Lord and become the cause of increased joy and delight to His Holiness Abraham, the Friend, in the exalted Kingdom.

order.why: Hear gratitude for Abraham’s descendants.
Consider the praise of steadfast faith in a particular community.
Read the garden and school images of spiritual inheritance.
Follow the invitation to read Isaiah through the hope of flowering.
Consider the account of glad tidings as a remedy for suffering.
Hear the call to awaken and guide through biblical imagery.
Read the wish to manifest the character of the prophets.
Consider becoming a lamp of guidance among Abraham’s descendants.
Close the linked readings with a journey compared to Isaiah’s life-giving service.
shortened: Your journey is of great importance, much like the journeys of Isaiah. The Prophet Isaiah traveled throughout the length and breadth of the Holy Land and bestowed a new vitality to the Israelites.

order.why: Retain the supplied account of messianic expectations with its existing catalogue status.

questions: How does the opening call to universal benefit reshape the meaning of belonging to a particular religious community?
What forms of spiritual education and human dignity are associated with Moses and the prophets?
How might attention to translation, genre, and historical setting change a reading of sacred scripture?
What does Isaiah 2:1–5 invite readers to imagine about instruction, the nations, and peace?
How can readers engage the collection’s polemical or reported passages while listening carefully to Jewish self-understanding?
What responsibilities might accompany a conviction that a prophetic promise is being fulfilled?

references.label: 1 · Isaiah 2:1–5 · Instruction and peace among the nations
references.note: Read verses 1–5 in Mechon Mamre’s Hebrew and English text. Isaiah’s vision brings the nations to divine instruction and portrays weapons becoming implements of cultivation. Compare its universal horizon with the opening call to benefit all humanity. Allow the biblical text its own voice rather than assuming that every reader shares the compilation’s interpretation of its fulfillment.

subjects.displayTitle: Work as worship: the spirit within the task
subjects.introduction: A person who makes a sheet of notepaper as well as it can be made, with full attention and an honest heart, is praising God. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá said so without irony, and Bahá’u’lláh had already raised the craft, the trade and the field to the rank of worship, so that the farmer bent over his furrow stands beside the worshipper bowed in a temple. Three things make the equation hold: the work must be useful to others, done with skill pursued toward excellence, and sprung from a pure intention. Idleness is refused, but so is a life swallowed by earning; the hands may be busy while the heart stays turned toward God, and a day holds room for labour, prayer, rest and the care of one’s health and family. The Bhagavad Gita’s counsel to act as a duty without attachment to the fruits of action belongs in this conversation, even though its account of spiritual attainment is its own [1]. The question is not only what we produce but whom it serves and what it makes of us. From here the path leads through useful occupation, the acquisition of a craft, and the fruit every life is asked to bring forth.
subjects.arc: Begin with a humble act of craftsmanship, explore intention and useful excellence, then connect livelihood with cooperation, remembrance, health, and the fruits of service.

order.why: Ground the inquiry in the command to work for one’s own and others’ benefit.
Open with making a piece of notepaper as a vivid example of worship.
shortened: The man who makes a piece of notepaper to the best of his ability, conscientiously, concentrating all his forces on perfecting it, is giving praise to God. Briefly, all effort and exertion put forth by man from the fullness of his heart is worship, if it is prompted by the highest motives and the will to do service to humanity.

order.why: State the relation of useful activity and a pure intention.
Bring the principle to the painter’s brush and the pursuit of excellence.
Set honest work beside prayer within a broader account of human unity.
Consider the equality of occupations when practiced with trustworthy conduct.
Read craftsmanship as a form of knowledge and wisdom.
shortened: One of the names of God is the Fashioner, and He has always loved and continues to love craftsmanship. Therefore, whoever among His servants manifests this name is beloved in the presence of the Wronged One. Craftsmanship is a volume from the volumes of divine knowledge and a treasure from the treasuries of divine wisdom.

order.why: Consider craftsmen through their practical benefit to society.
Hear the affirmation of craft and trade as worship.
Read the gift of craftsmanship as an occasion for gratitude.
Consider earning through a profession as nearness to God.
Retain the concise affirmation of the craftsman’s work.
shortened: The craft of every craftsman is accounted as worship. This is among the great favors of the Lord for His servants.

order.why: Read the corresponding statement linking profession and worship.
shortened: In this great dispensation, art (or a profession) is identical with an act of worship and this is a clear text of the Blessed Perfection.

order.why: Keep the direct affirmation of labor as devotion.
Hear the reported description of a day of service as prayer.
shortened: "That is well. Very well. A day's work done in the spirit of service is in itself an act of worship. Such work is a prayer unto God."

order.why: Explicitly accounts the work of craftsmen as worship.
Read the reported formulation emphasizing the spirit of service.
Retain the brief reported declaration to an artist.
shortened: A painter asked: "Is art a worthy vocation?" Abdu'l-Baha turning to her impressively, said: "Art is worship."

order.why: Consider the reported connection between trustworthiness and human advancement.
Read the reported call to express divine qualities through one’s best work.
shortened: Man must work and in that work show the qualities of GOD and thus do good. His work, both material and spiritual, must show what he is. By his arts, sciences, inventions and all of his work he must show his best ability.

order.why: Explore occupations as opportunities to demonstrate spiritual qualities.
Read farming through good intention, trustworthiness, and effort.
Consider agricultural skill through the comfort it can provide to many.
shortened: Agriculture is a noble science and, should thy son become proficient in this field, he will become a means of providing for the comfort of untold numbers of people.

order.why: Connect mastery of agriculture with learning as worship.
Read teaching as worship through care for spiritual children.
shortened: It followeth that teachers are servants of the Lord God, since they have arisen to perform this task, which is the same as worship. You must therefore offer praise with every breath, for you are educating your spiritual children.

order.why: Consider the education of girls and boys as a shared responsibility.
shortened: The first duty of God's friends and the handmaidens of the All-Merciful is to strive by whatever means possible for the education and training of children, both male and female.

order.why: Keep the reported practical educational advice in its historical setting.
shortened: The parents must exert their utmost effort;- thus their children may learn trades and professions. The first and primal thing that is essential for every young man is a trade. This is supremely an industrial age and the man who has not specialized himself in some line, will be crippled on every side and hampered on every step in his pursuit of a livelihood. No sooner the children have laid the foundation of their theoretic and primary knowledge in the school-rooms they must be sent to the workshops to learn the applied and practical sciences.

order.why: Read the wish for both personal perfections and a learned craft.
Consider proficiency as an essential part of the craft’s spiritual character.
Hear the encouragement to excel in one’s particular profession.
Read diligence through the image of the Kingdom’s marketplace.
Consider the reported call to perfect even coarse straw matting.
Read the striking image of each thing’s paradise as its perfection.
Hear the recognition of an actual crafted gift.
shortened: God, exalted be His glory, has loved to witness pleasing crafts from His loved ones. Blessed art thou for what thou hast crafted has been presented before the face of thy Lord, the Wronged One, the Stranger.
God willing, may each of the loved ones be enabled to manifest a craft from among the crafts and be assisted in that which they have been commanded in the Book of God, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Consider the remembered craftsman and the acceptance of useful work.
Read gratitude for having perfected a learned art.
Hear arts and crafts described as means of nearness.
Consider the reported encouragement to persist in one’s art.
Read the reported happiness of seeing work brought to completion.
Keep the reported emphasis on love for one’s vocation.
Consider the reported value of constancy in practical affairs.
Read commercial skill and effort within the specific advice about partnership.
Explore cooperation among craftspeople as a way to express divine qualities.
shortened: Therefore, if several of the friends of God who dwell in any of the cities of truth and who are engaged in the same craft were to unite and work together in partnership, seeking from God the grace to conduct their dealings according to divine qualities, then surely from their behavior would shine forth the light of the Sun of Truth, and their craft and occupation would truly acquire the character of worship.

order.why: Connect practical work with consultation and mutual assistance.
shortened: Therefore be confident in divine protection and assistance, and seek confirmation from Him, and consult together in all matters both small and great, even regarding agriculture, crafts, commerce and livelihood - each one should repeatedly consult and assist, for consultation is among the divine commands and the cause of complete victory in affairs, attracting divine assistance and grace.

order.why: Hear the reported call for rich and poor to work with their fellows.
Read the reported agricultural advice beside its call to upright conduct.
shortened: They are most industrious and you can ameliorate your conditions and increase your crop by watching their ways.
Live a virtuous, upright, honest, truthful life.

order.why: Consider the reported relation of useful affairs to awareness and responsibility.
shortened: The other kind are those affairs which contribute toward the maintenance of livelihood, adding to the comfort, happiness and progress of the human family. Spiritual powers always come to the assistance of such affairs, they increase the moral insight and responsibility of man and add to his awareness and mindfulness."

order.why: Connect livelihood with lifting the burdens of others.
shortened: It must not be implied that one should give up avocation and attainment to livelihood. On the contrary, in the Cause of Baha'u'llah monasticism and asceticism are not sanctioned. In this great Cause the light of guidance is shining and radiant. Baha'u'llah has even said that occupation and labor are devotion. All humanity must obtain a livelihood by sweat of the brow and bodily exertion, at the same time seeking to lift the burden of others, striving to be the source of comfort to souls and facilitating the means of living. This in itself is devotion to God.

order.why: Retain the reported affirmation of a right to work and joy.
Read the reported purpose of work as dignity and self-assurance.
Consider occupation as relief from dwelling on unpleasant matters.
Read the call to earn a livelihood in its original address.
Retain the related injunction and hope for assistance.
Consider the responsibility to contribute rather than impose avoidable burdens.
shortened: Such idle souls are certainly not acceptable, for every soul must pursue some work, craft or profession so that they may carry their own weight rather than becoming a burden for others to bear, like a paralyzing nightmare.

order.why: Read the reported pairing of a profession with an exemplary life.
shortened: Every person must have a profession, whether it be literary or manual, and must live a clean, manly, honest life, an example of purity to be imitated by others.

order.why: Consider personal effort beside the impermanence of inherited wealth.
Contrast a legitimately earned coin with improperly acquired treasure.
Read the reported social value of rightly acquired and administered wealth.
Consider benefit to others and oneself within a limit on greed.
shortened: However, engagement therein for the benefit of the servants of God and for one's own benefit to an extent that does not lead to the fire of greed and passion has been and is praiseworthy. The King of the Messengers - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for His sake - has said: "The one who earns his living is beloved of God."

order.why: Ask what moral fruit a particular form of commerce or craft produces.
Read the condition that earning must not displace remembrance.
Keep the reported caution against making livelihood one’s entire ambition.
shortened: It is true that man must work, engage in an occupation so that he may not become a burden on the community but all his ambition must not revolve around this.

order.why: Consider the limits of temporal harvests.
Read the reported insistence that work and prescribed prayer support one another.
Hear the reported example of Peter and a heart turned toward God.
shortened: No occupation can prevent the soul coming to God. Peter was a fisherman, yet he accomplished most wonderful things; but the heart must be turned always towards God, no matter what the work is; this is the important things: and then the power of God will work in us.

order.why: Consider the reported image of working hands and an attentive heart.
Read the reported pairing of occupation and detachment.
Keep the particular reported division of a day as its own counsel.
Read the reported concern for a teacher’s health and renewal.
shortened: A teacher shall sleep at night with the thought that the next day he may be refreshed in order to do his duty more fully in relation to teaching his pupils. Therefore Mrs.--must take good care of her health. Just look at Mr.--'s very good health--see how much work he can do, how much work he can stand! Whatever work is referred to him, he can discharge it fully.

order.why: Connect health, work, and service in the reported account.
Keep the reported wood-chopping image as a reflection on recurring effort.
shortened: In this world we are all more or less wood-choppers. If we are attacked with a sickness and survive it we have to work a little more, to chop a few more loads of woods and the world will go on perennially.

order.why: Retain the reported blacksmith anecdote as an anecdote, not an instruction about labor conditions.
Read the explicit responsibility to provide for and communicate with family.
shortened: Praise be to God that they have been aided to follow God's command, for all are enjoined to engage in craft, trade and agriculture. However, they must act according to what hath been revealed in the Book - that is, they should send something to their families and inform them. These deeds which all are commanded to perform in God's Book have been and shall ever be the cause of glory and the source of blessing and the manifestation of bounty.

order.why: Consider the specific advice about work, economy, and debt.
shortened: Trust in God and engage in your work and practice economy; the confirmations of God shall descend and you will be enabled to pay off your debts.

order.why: Pair practical engagement with trust in God.
shortened: As for material matters, you should engage in work while placing your trust in God. He will send down to you from the heaven of His favors that which is ordained for you.

order.why: Hear the corresponding concise counsel to work with trust.
shortened: Occupy thyself with some occupation, placing thy trust in God, the All-Wise, for all are commanded to engage in some occupation.

order.why: Distinguish the worker’s action from hoped-for blessing.
shortened: God, exalted be His glory, hath commanded engagement in craft, earning, and trade. Yours is the action, and His is the blessing and loving-kindness.

order.why: Read the injunction to occupy oneself while trusting God.
shortened: In this Most Great Revelation, engagement in some occupation hath been prescribed for all the loved ones. Be thou occupied with some matter, placing thy trust in God.

order.why: Retain the personal advice to return and become familiar with work.
shortened: Now place your trust in God and return to the regions of Iran, and engage in some occupation and become familiar with some work.

order.why: Hear the encouragement to practice a profession with confidence in grace.
Read the brief assurance accompanying work in a craft.
Retain the counsel to work without remissness and its source omission.
shortened: After it was read before His presence, He said: "Let them place their trust in God in all matters and occupy themselves with their work.
Be not remiss in thy work.

order.why: Hear the prayer for comfort and steadfastness in occupation.
Read the prayer that business bring what is good for its practitioner.
Consider the consolation offered for engagement in outward affairs.
Hear joy at obedience through learning and practicing a craft.
shortened: This matter was the cause of greatest joy, for all are commanded to engage in a craft, which is indeed accounted as worship before God.

order.why: Retain the brief commendation of crafts and professions.
shortened: The occupation that is beloved in the sight of God is engagement in crafts and professions.

order.why: Read the general duty to work even during a short stay.
shortened: Regarding agriculture, He has given a general ruling in these matters, which is that it is obligatory for every soul to engage in a profession, agriculture, or craft, and that very work itself is worship in the sight of God, even if one tarries but a day in any land.

order.why: Keep the festival-related instruction and its existing attribution.
Retain the simple personal instruction to engage in commerce.
Hear the reported determination to earn through one’s own labor.
Consider the honor given to the deed of working.
shortened: All servants have been commanded to pursue an occupation in God's Book. Praise be to God that ye have attained this supreme gift. I swear by the Sun of divine utterance that this deed of yours is more glorious in the sight of God than the deeds of those who count themselves among the pillars of the earth. God Himself hath testified and doth testify to this truth.

order.why: Read the concise description of work accepted by God and people.
shortened: God willing, he will strive earnestly to learn and acquire crafts. This is a work through which a person becomes beloved and regarded both with God and with people.

order.why: Connect continuing a profession with service to the Kingdom.
Read conduct and character as ways to serve wherever one is.
Keep the reported practice of freely giving what was received.
Consider the reported hope for spiritual influence on commerce and politics.
Close with the reported daily relationship of love, work, prayer, peace, and joy.

questions: What changes when a familiar task is approached as a possible act of worship?
How do intention, competence, honesty, and benefit to others work together in these passages?
What distinguishes pursuing excellence from allowing work or earning to absorb the whole of life?
How might the Gita’s teaching on action without attachment illuminate the relation between effort and its results?
What forms of cooperation and consultation could make a workplace more expressive of service?
How could prayer, rest, learning, and practical work support one another in an ordinary week?

references.label: 1 · Bhagavad Gita 3.19 · Action without attachment
references.note: Read verse 3.19 in A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada’s 1972 translation, distinguishing the verse from the commentary that follows it. Compare duty without attachment to results with the compilation’s calls to work wholeheartedly, serve others, and keep the heart free. Consider both the shared inquiry into action and the distinct spiritual frameworks in which the teachings are expressed.

subjects.displayTitle: The divine gardener: patience, care, and the fruits of growth
subjects.introduction: A gardener whose own heart is not a garden, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá said, cannot raise a single flower. The image runs deep in His teaching: the Prophets are the Gardeners of human souls, turning jungles into orchards, straightening crooked branches, and drawing out what God has already placed within every person. Their garden is not uniform. Flowers of every colour and scent, watered by one rain and warmed by one sun, make its beauty precisely through their difference. Growth takes patience; a man ploughing bare ground in winter looks foolish to a passer-by who has never seen a harvest. Children above all are fresh saplings, and their education is among the most meritorious of human acts. In the Gospel of John the Father tends the vine and prunes the branches so that they bear more fruit [1]. Whoever receives such care is asked in turn to water others. From here the way leads to the Manifestation as Educator and as divine Physician, to the soul as soil, and to prayers that ask for children to grow fresh and fair.
subjects.arc: Begin with the heart’s garden and its varied flowers, follow divine care through growth and renewal, then explore education, patient service, loss, and the fruits of a cultivated life.

order.why: Establish a garden whose variety contributes to shared beauty.
shortened: The Kingdom of God is like a flower garden adorned with various sweet-scented flowers, blossoms, herbs and trees. Since they are under the training of one Gardener, are watered from one water, are nurtured by the heat of one sun, receive bounty from one breeze, and grow from one soil, their different colors, compositions, forms, shapes, tastes and fragrances cause the adornment and splendor of one another.

order.why: Open with the reported relation between an inner garden and the care one can offer.
Read cultivation as bringing forth capacities already entrusted to humanity.
shortened: In one of the Tablets this most exalted Word was revealed: All the Prophets and chosen ones were commanded by God, exalted be His glory, to water the trees of human existence with the living waters of refinement and wisdom, that there might appear from all that which God hath deposited within man.

order.why: Name the Manifestations as cultivators of hearts and souls.
Bring the image to the loving education of a child.
shortened: If a child be trained from his infancy, he will, through the loving care of the Holy Gardener, drink in the crystal waters of the spirit and of knowledge, like a young tree amid the rilling brooks. And certainly he will gather to himself the bright rays of the Sun of Truth, and through its light and heat will grow ever fresh and fair in the garden of life.

order.why: Consider fruit as the purpose of planting and nurture.
Read the reported winter scene as a lesson in unseen growth.
shortened: See in the winter how bare and lifeless the trees and plants seem, without leaves and without fruit. Suppose one should pass by at this time who knew nothing of the condition of the earth and saw a man ploughing it up and casting grain in the furrow. Would he not say, "How foolish this man is. He is troubling himself for no result, working for no purpose and wasting that which would give him food"? But in due time the showers descend upon the earth, the sun shines, the breezes blow and we see the result in great beauty and production.

order.why: Consider delayed harvest through the text’s account of Christ’s influence.
Retain the concise identification of prophets as gardeners.
Read the public address’s transformation from thorny ground to orchard.
Follow the gradual cultivation described in the public address.
Read the need for skilled care in transforming the human garden.
shortened: The world of mankind is in need of expert gardeners who may convert these forests into delectable rose gardens, may substitute for these barren trees ones that yield fruit, and may replace these useless weeds with roses and fragrant herbs.

order.why: Read education as the removal of obstacles to fruitful growth.
Keep the reported account of Christ’s cultivation and its source omission.
Consider the reported goal of full growth and fruit.
Read the reported relation between prophetic education and human advancement.
Hear the reported restoration of order through the gardener’s instructions.
shortened: The kingdom of God is likened unto a garden and the gardener is a blessed Manifestation. The gardener comes and finds the trees unfruitful and the garden in disorder. Through his instructions order is restored and the trees become fruitful.

order.why: Consider the reported heart as a place requiring cultivation.
shortened: The heart of man is a garden. The real garden is in order, well planted, watered and cultivated. This is not so with the jungle. The jungle gives no evidence of cultivation. Where there is no gardener disorder prevails. Wild growth produces nothing.

order.why: Read the reported contrast between a cared-for garden and neglect.
Join the reported images of sunlight and active cultivation.
Consider the reported possibility of restoring stunted growth.
shortened: But if the jungle falls into the hands of a gardener fruitless trees will be grafted by him and become fruitful. Or if the trees have been stunted by neglect, yielding poor fruits, the care of the gardener transforms them, causing them to produce delicate and luscious fruits.

order.why: Read the reported need for continued care after an initial transformation.
Retain the related reported warning about neglect.
Hear the brief reported blessing on trees that receive training.
shortened: In the forest there are numerous trees; but blessed are the trees which are trained by the gardener.

order.why: Uses the Divine Gardener and a fruitful tree to explain faith, piety and deeds.
Consider the reported increase of capacity under sustained care.
shortened: Every soul that enters under the shadow of Baha'u'llah, day by day their capacity increases, like a tree that is under the care of a perfect gardener - it will surely grow and develop and achieve perfect cultivation.

order.why: Read the assurance of continuing education.
Explore the many forms of nurture in a single extended image.
Hear gratitude for having been planted and watered.
Read the sapling’s dependence on bounty and grace.
Consider growth as an occasion for collective praise.
shortened: O peerless saplings of the rose-garden of the love of God! Praise ye God that in these divine gardens ye are trees planted by the hand of providence, and through God's infinite bounty ye have grown and flourished.

order.why: Read the image of human souls as incomparable saplings.
shortened: That is, human souls are like incomparable saplings that have sprouted from that blessed earth. With the hand of ancient power, those blessed and approved trees were planted in the vineyard.

order.why: Keep the reported account of planting, knowledge, and protection.
shortened: They are the trees planted by the sacred hand of Baha'u'llah in the orchard of the Kingdom. He hath watered you with the rivers of His knowledge and hath protected you from winds and storms.

order.why: Read the reported invitation to deepen one’s roots.
shortened: The Cause of the Blessed Perfection is a garden of infinite beauty and attraction. From amongst the people He elected us and as His tender plants He planted us with His own Holy hand in this divine garden. The rays of His educative sun shone upon us, the showers of the Clouds of His Generosity poured over us, the breezes of His Providence wafted by us;- so that we may grow and develop and send down our roots deeper and deeper into the heart of the earth.

order.why: Hear gratitude for desirable saplings already planted.
shortened: Praise be to God that through the confirmation of the true Gardener, fine and desirable saplings have been planted.

order.why: Consider the heart’s avenues as places of newly designed beauty.
shortened: Praise be to God, the Gardener of Providence has engaged in designing the flowers of truth in the avenue of the friends' hearts.

order.why: Read the garden of knowledge through its flowers and fragrance.
shortened: The Gardener of Oneness hath designed such flower beds of divine knowledge in the avenues of hearts as to inspire the envy of all possible gardens, and in the meadow of divine wisdom's mysteries, such blossoms have opened that their holy fragrances have perfumed the horizons.

order.why: Look toward the anticipated flowering of meanings in human hearts.
shortened: O thou esteemed one: This world is like unto a forest, and its trees are fruitless. Now the Divine Gardener hath come in order to make this unfruitful forest a Divine Garden and increase its trees in fruit yield, through Divine training. Before long thou shalt see how this Gardener will engage in adorning the avenues of hearts withe the flowers of Significances, and make the trees full of blossoms and fruits.

order.why: Hear the affirmation of continual growth from the spring of mercy.
shortened: In every hour, whatever the Divine Farmer has planted in the field of being and watered from the spring of mercy grows green and flourishing, becoming the beauty of the rose garden and the freshness of the orchard.

order.why: Read the sowing of reality within the field of existence.
Retain the concise celebration of the garden’s Lord.
Consider the labor and suffering attributed to the heavenly Farmer.
Read the reported renewal of divine springtime.
Distinguish new planting from the impossible revival described in the old-tree analogy.
Keep the reported comparison with the Mosaic tree attributed as a theological interpretation.
Retain the reported account of Persia’s renewal in its historical voice.
shortened: The example of Persia is like unto a garden which has been taken out of the cultivating hand of the gardener. The wild animals have run through its pastures, its meadows are turned upside down, its trees are leafless, its plants are dried and its tender, fragrant flowers trod under foot; to such an extent that whereas formerly it was a rose-garden it has now become a thorny patch. But when the real gardener appears he takes the garden again under his care and arrange [sic] it better than its former condition.

order.why: Read the combination of physician and cultivator as an image of remedy.
Consider the protection of a tree through removal of withered branches.
Read the reported condition of recognizing the true gardener before trusting the act.
Keep the reported protective-weeding analogy and its source gap visible.
Retain the brief reported judgment of deficient plants without broadening its application.
Compare the reported potter’s workshop with cultivation as formation.
shortened: As the potter from his clay makes a vessel to his honour, for general advantage and use, he forms, presses, kneads, pinches, fires, cleanses, cools it (all from the inside and outside), so are we in the workshop of the Creator. - He, the Almighty and All-Wise, the Knower and the Able, the Willing and the Acting, the Advisor and the Executor, is at work, at His work, to make something of us, for His honour, for the temporal and eternal advantage and use of the vessel.

order.why: Hear the image of transplantation as consolation concerning loss.
shortened: Thou shalt see their faces in the highest heavens, for when the loving Gardener cherishes a plant, He removes it from among other plants and transfers it from a confined space to a vast field and a beautiful, flourishing garden where that plant may grow, extend its branches, unfold its flowers, yield its fruit and spread its shade.

order.why: Read the corresponding reported story with its limits on human understanding.
Bring the reported gardener image to the work of teachers.
Consider children’s education as service within the divine orchard.
shortened: No greater service can be imagined, in this day, than the education and training of Baha'i children as it ought to be done, inasmuch as this service is like unto gardening in the Divine orchard.

order.why: Retain the concise address to a teacher of young children.
Read early schooling through the formation of manners and spiritual qualities.
Keep the reported account of children’s development and training attributed.
shortened: Now, these children are fresh plants which have fallen into the hands of the gardener. Therefore, they will be very well educated; they will become fruitful trees; they will become very blessed trees; they will become most delectable trees. The Gardener is blessed, and the skill of the Gardener will become manifest in them.

order.why: Hear the reported gratitude for a children’s garden in the West.
shortened: In San Francisco, through the hand of the Gardener of God, who has appeared in the Orient, to see such a garden as the result of His handiwork in the West -- this is a source of great thanksgiving in the East. Hence I am hopeful, through the favors of that Real Gardener, that He may ever care for these trees, and water them; that He may ever refresh, through His Holy Dewdrops, His flowers; may shower upon them from His clouds of Mercy.

order.why: Read the father’s duty through kindness, favor, and prayer.
Consider the hope that a branch will flourish like its root.
shortened: In the gathering of hearts you occupy the seat of highest respect, and in reality of souls you deserve complete honor. You are the descendant of that illustrious one and the fruit of that supreme paradise garden. Therefore we are expectant and hopeful, watchful and in intense anticipation that this delicate branch, like its noble root, will become fruitful with the utmost freshness and grace, and will gain verdancy and vitality from the life-giving breezes, and will become the ornament and adornment of the divine garden and yield perpetual fruit.

order.why: Read the hoped-for joy that growing descendants bring to their family.
Consider caring for a planting left by someone who has died.
shortened: I hope that the descendants will bring honor to their ancestors, so that they may water and nurture the sapling that that one ascended unto God planted, until it casts a mighty shade and yields fresh fruits and produce.

order.why: Hear a child’s prayer for mercy and the breath of springtime.
Retain the prayer that names dependence on the Gardener.
shortened: O Kind God! Though we are helpless children and weak infants, distressed and without direction, yet we are saplings of Thy garden and Thou art the Gardener.

order.why: Read the prayer for a new flower’s freshness and education.
Hear the hope for leaves, blossoms, and desired fruit.
Read the petition for abundant growth and spreading branches.
Consider nurture through the rains of grace and breezes of the Covenant.
Hear the communal prayer for growth and benefit beyond description.
shortened: We beseech God that He may keep those illumined hearts alive and fresh at all times through the breaths of the spirit and fragrant breezes, and that the pure seed which the divine Husbandman has scattered in that field may, through the education of the outpouring of the April rain of the All-Merciful's mercy and the heat of the rays of the Sun of the horizon of inner meanings, sprout forth and become verdant and fresh through the moisture of the dew, yielding bounty, blessing, increase and benefit beyond description.

order.why: Read the prayer for a garden of meaning within thought and speech.
Keep the reported vocation of sowing wisdom in hearts.
Consider the farmer’s preparation of soil, seed, and water.
Read the reported sower analogy and the question of an enduring harvest.
shortened: All souls are farmers, but some farm in commerce, some in industry, and some in politics - all grow green but have no lasting blessing or eternal benefit except spiritual farming and heavenly guidance. Observe how the seed that Christ scattered still bears fruit. That is why He said My word is like seeds scattered by the farmer's hand. The seeds that fall on the path and among weeds and on rocks have no fruit or result, but what is scattered on good soil grows and bears fruit and becomes a source of blessing.

order.why: Hear the encouragement to teach through the image of good seed and soil.
shortened: Teaching in that region is like when a skilled farmer sows pure seed in pure soil. Surely the clouds of the Most Glorious Kingdom will rain down, the heat of the Sun of Reality will cause growth, the breeze of grace will nurture, and magnificent results will be achieved.

order.why: Follow the passage from receiving seed to becoming a skilled cultivator.
shortened: The heavenly Farmer scattered fresh seed in that soil, and the celestial cloud gave water, and the Sun of Reality bestowed warmth.
I hope that this pure seed will soon sprout and form heap upon heap of harvest, and that you will become a skilled farmer in this divine field and be the cause of acquiring bounty and blessing.

order.why: Consider the responsibility of watering entrusted to others.
Read cultivation through universal love and the removal of estrangement.
Hear the invitation to become a farmer of reality within humanity.
shortened: I hope that you may become baptized with the Fire of the Love of God and the Water of the Holy Spirit, and that each of you may become a Divine Farmer and sow in the farm of humanity the seeds of reality, irrigating them with the Waters of the Teacings of Baha'u'llah, so that the Light of Truth may illumine that country.

order.why: Consider gardeners’ self-giving care for the growth of others.
Connect cultivation with enlightening deeds and words.
Read the hope for two people’s active cooperation in the vineyard.
shortened: Through the bounties of God do I cherish this hope that they will become two active gardeners in the vineyard of God and will become illumined with the light of the Heavenly Confirmations.

order.why: Consider the honor given to the cultivator actively sowing.
Read present service through the future shade and fruit of a tree.
shortened: Today whosoever is engaged in the service of the Cause of God he is like a gardener who is planting a tree. Ere long that tree shall grow and develop, giving cool shade to all parts and producing most luscious fruits.

order.why: Keep the reported practical sequence of labor before harvest.
shortened: Dost thou see the farmers furrowing the fields for the sowing of new seeds? Are they not working with tireless exertion? If they do not plough the ground, if they do not sow the seeds, if they do not look after them and pull out the tares and weeds, if they do not water the soil, will they gather any crops? No.
In serving the Cause of God we must ever keep the example of the farmers before our eyes.

order.why: Consider the responsibility to sow well before expecting a harvest.
Read the reported confidence in seeds developing toward fruition.
shortened: The principles of the Baha'i Cause are the pure seeds which we are sowing in the fertile ground. Unquestionably many harvests shall be gathered. Daily these seeds are sprouting, growing in size and verdancy and soon they will reach the stage of fruition.

order.why: Keep the reported transition from cultivating a garden to singing within it.
Read the adjacent shepherd image through nourishment by knowledge and wisdom.
Consider the Holy Shepherd’s sacrificial care beside the gardener’s labor.
Return to the reported connection between careful nurture and better fruit.
Read the qualities that make a garden worthy of its name.
shortened: O friends of the All-Glorious Lord!

A garden requires graceful trees, wondrous fruits, delicate flowers, divine fragrances, roses and nightingales and hyacinths. Until such a garden is adorned thus, and such trees bear fruit, and such life-giving fruits are cultivated, it will not become a garden or a rose garden.

order.why: Consider fruit through the sweetness and delight it offers others.
Keep the reported warning that nurture calls for a fruitful response.
Read steadfastness through the scriptural test of fruits.
shortened: O thou who hast diffused the fragrances of truth! Stand thou firm in the Cause of God like unto a tree firmly rooted, with massive trunk, spreading branches and abundant fruits, that thou mayest become the manifestation of that which the glorious Lord hath said in the Gospel: "By their fruits ye shall know them."

order.why: Hear the reported delight in a flower sharing its fragrance.
shortened: The gardener is pleased with the flower that is diffusing its fragrance. The nostrils are perfumed by its sweet smell.

order.why: Close with the reported unfinished bouquet and the gardener still at work.
shortened: Again, the Lord of the Kingdom is like a gardener.  He plants in the garden many flowers of various colors, puts them together like this bunch (referring to one on the table).  So we are waiting and expecting to finish this bunch."
(After a pause.)
"At present the gardener is working."

questions: What does the gardener image reveal about growth that an image of instant change might overlook?
How can shared nurture strengthen differences of character and capacity rather than erase them?
What might soil, water, light, pruning, and fruit correspond to in education or inner life?
How does John 15:1–8 deepen or complicate the image, especially through its different roles for Father, vine, and branches?
What responsibilities arise when people who have received care become cultivators of others’ growth?
How might patience, grief, and hope change when the full harvest of an effort cannot yet be seen?

references.label: 1 · John 15:1–8 · Vine, branches, and the cultivator
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of abiding, pruning, and bearing fruit. The Father is the cultivator, Jesus the vine, and disciples the branches. Compare these relationships with the compilation’s different uses of the gardener image, especially divine education and human participation. Ask what both passages imply about dependence, care, and the visible results of spiritual life.
